name: SETL
summary: Very-high-level language from NYU's Courant Institute built on finite sets, maps and tuples with set formers and quantifiers; used for executable specifications (Ada/Ed) and a direct ancestor of ABC and Python.

level_notes.0: GNU SETL (David Bacon) is the maintained implementation; historical CIMS SETL (LITTLE-based) and SETL2 sources are preserved at softwarepreservation.org. SetlX and ISETL are dialect interpreters.
level_notes.1: No standard; Dewar's 1979 "The SETL Programming Language" and the 1975 interim report are the classic definitions, Condict (1983) gives a denotational semantics, and the GNU SETL manuals define the modern dialect (its Language Reference is a stub).
level_notes.2: Most historical tutorials, papers and theses are scanned at the Computer History Museum Software Preservation Group site.
level_notes.3: Wikipedia, PLDB, Rosetta Code, and the SPG history page.
